behavioral_effects: The active branch gets conflict-independent CI: governance job (check, selftest, sync-no-op, gate smoke, coverage), lint, tests, security scan run on every push
compatibility_impact: CI now also runs on pushes to fullstack2; main and master triggers unchanged; PR checks against main unaffected
limitations: This is the first CI run of the governance job on a Linux runner from this branch; cross-platform determinism is designed in (LF-only writer, sorted keys, POSIX paths) but this push is its first live proof
reason: PR checks cannot run while the PR into main has merge conflicts - GitHub builds pull_request workflows on a test merge commit that a conflicted PR cannot produce - and the push trigger only watched main and master, so the active development branch had no CI at all. Adding fullstack2 to the push trigger gives the branch its own conflict-independent CI runs while the excluded-range decision on the PR remains open
rollback: git revert removes fullstack2 from the trigger list
security_impact: None - CI trigger scope only; no job content changed
summary: CI runs on pushes to fullstack2

validators_run.evidence_ref: not run for this change - a CI trigger list cannot affect test behavior; the real validation is the workflow run this push starts, watched to completion below
